How to read a set:

| Table | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Vocabulary | The qualifier values the set's fields use, and what each means |
| Requirements | How strongly a consumer needs a kind on each level: `required`, `recommended`, `optional` |
| Coverage | One matrix per level: ✓ where a software version has the field, · where not |
| Fields | Every catalogued field once, sorted by kind; `apb-catalog table` writes the same as CSV |

| Location | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `layers` | One value per run and feature |
| `var` | One value per feature, across the experiment |
| `obs` | One value per run |

A qualifier value `unknown` means the evidence does not establish it; a lookup that would depend on it raises `UnresolvedField` instead of guessing.

## `abundance_alpha`

- Covers every layer an APB2 rule marks with the role `abundance`; a test keeps the two equal
- `normalization` is fixed per column: `none` never normalized, `run_setting` as the run's settings chose; which method a run used is not catalogued
- Keys name kind and normalization together: `intensity`, `normalized_intensity`, `intensity_unknown_normalization`; asking `intensity` where the normalization is unknown answers unknown
- `unknown` kind: Spectronaut's `PG.Quantity`, MSAngel's protein-set abundances
- `unknown` normalization: FragPipe, MetaMorpheus, quantms, i2MassChroQ, Sage, pb_custom
- Left out: DIA-NN's `Genes.MaxLFQ`, a gene-group quantity

<!-- generated by scripts/coverage_tables.py: abundance_alpha -->

### Vocabulary

| Qualifier | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `intensity` | A measured signal of the level's feature, summed, integrated or at apex, or a value combined from lower-level features' signals, as aggregation says; ms_level says whether it is measured on MS1 or on MS2. |
| `kind` | `ibaq` | Intensity-based absolute quantification: summed intensity divided by the number of theoretically observable peptides. |
| `normalization` | `none` | The software never normalizes this column. |
| `normalization` | `run_setting` | The column carries whatever cross-run normalization the run's settings chose, possibly none, as DIA-NN's Normalised columns do. |
| `normalization` | `unknown` | The evidence does not establish it. |
| `aggregation` | `none` | Measured on the feature's own signal, such as a precursor's peak area; nothing is combined. |
| `aggregation` | `sum` | The sum of the lower-level features' signals, as MaxQuant's Intensity columns. |
| `aggregation` | `top_n` | From the most intense lower-level features, as DIA-NN's Top N (default N = 1, the most intense precursor). |
| `aggregation` | `maxlfq` | MaxLFQ: delayed normalization and maximal peptide-ratio extraction (Cox et al. 2014). |
| `aggregation` | `directlfq` | directLFQ (Ammar et al. 2023). |
| `aggregation` | `unknown` | The evidence does not establish it. |
| `ms_level` | `ms1` | Measured on the precursor's MS1 signal, as DDA tools quantify. |
| `ms_level` | `ms2` | Measured on MS2 fragment signals, as DIA tools quantify. |
| `ms_level` | `unknown` | The evidence does not establish it. |

## `apb_alpha`

- Fields `apb2 convert` writes itself, so no vendor review is needed; `apb-catalog check apb_alpha` checks every packaged rule level against the requirements
- `peptidoform` is only `recommended` on the peptidoform level: MaxQuant's has no modification positions
- `peptidoform_fragment` is only `recommended`: Spectronaut keys fragments on its own columns
- A role names the var column the level's rule marks

<!-- generated by scripts/coverage_tables.py: apb_alpha -->

### Vocabulary

| Qualifier | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `peptide` | The plain amino-acid sequence: ProForma_peptide (PSI-MS MS:1000888, stripped peptide sequence). |
| `kind` | `peptidoform` | The sequence with its modifications in ProForma notation: ProForma_peptidoform (PSI-MS MS:1003169, proforma peptidoform sequence). |
| `kind` | `peptidoform_unlocalized` | The sequence with modifications whose positions the vendor does not report, as ProForma unknown-position groups: ProForma_peptidoform_unlocalized, which MaxQuant's peptidoform level writes instead of ProForma_peptidoform. |
| `kind` | `peptidoform_ion` | The peptidoform with its charge: ProForma_ion (PSI-MS MS:1003270, proforma peptidoform ion notation). |
| `kind` | `peptidoform_fragment` | A fragment of a peptidoform ion: ProForma_ion with the fragment label, ProForma_fragment. |
| `kind` | `decoy` | Whether the vendor marks the feature as a decoy: apb_Decoy. |
| `kind` | `contaminant` | Whether the vendor marks the feature as a contaminant it flags or adds itself: apb_Contaminant. |
| `kind` | `protein_assignment` | The protein or protein group the vendor assigns the feature to: the var column the level's rule marks with the role protein_assignment. |
| `kind` | `fasta_accessions` | The FASTA accessions the vendor lists for the feature: the var column the level's rule marks with the role fasta_accessions. |

| --- | --- | --- |

## `chromatography_alpha`

- Measured, aligned, predicted and library retention times are separate kinds and not interchangeable
- `aligned`: MaxQuant's calibrated RT, Proline's corrected time, DIA-NN's `Predicted.iRT`, Spectronaut's `EG.iRTEmpirical`
- `predicted`: DIA-NN's `Predicted.RT`, Spectronaut's `EG.RTPredicted`, AlphaDIA's `rt.calibrated`
- `unit=irt` is a scale, not a time: it never converts to seconds
- `unit=unknown`: FragPipe (instrument-dependent), AlphaPept (input-dependent), AlphaDIA peak widths (counted in cycles)
- Values are returned unchanged; the consumer converts the unit
- Where a vendor does not document a column, the entry carries the best reading and its evidence says so

<!-- generated by scripts/coverage_tables.py: chromatography_alpha -->

### Vocabulary

| Qualifier | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `retention_time` | Where the feature eluted in this run, measured on the run's own time axis: the apex or centre of its elution peak. |
| `kind` | `aligned_retention_time` | The measured retention time, moved by the software's alignment onto a scale shared by all runs: a reference run's time axis or the library's iRT scale. |
| `kind` | `predicted_retention_time` | Where the software expects the feature to elute in this run, from its library or prediction model calibrated to the run; not a measurement. |
| `kind` | `library_retention_time` | The spectral library's reference retention time, the same in every run. |
| `kind` | `mean_apex_retention_time` | A mean of apex times the software reports beside its apex retention time; what it averages over is not established. |
| `kind` | `ms2_retention_time` | The time of the MS/MS spectrum that identified the feature, rather than the apex of its elution peak. |
| `kind` | `peak_start` | Where the feature's elution peak begins, on the run's own time axis. |
| `kind` | `peak_end` | Where the feature's elution peak ends, on the run's own time axis. |
| `kind` | `aligned_peak_start` | Where the elution peak begins, on the aligned scale of aligned_retention_time. |
| `kind` | `aligned_peak_end` | Where the elution peak ends, on the aligned scale of aligned_retention_time. |
| `kind` | `peak_fwhm` | The width of the elution peak at half its maximum height. |
| `kind` | `aligned_peak_fwhm` | The width at half maximum, on the aligned scale of aligned_retention_time. |
| `kind` | `peak_width` | The full width of the elution peak, from its start to its end. |
| `unit` | `second` | Seconds; multiply by 1 to express the value in QPX seconds. |
| `unit` | `minute` | Minutes; multiply by 60 to express the value in QPX seconds. |
| `unit` | `irt` | Indexed retention time: the dimensionless scale of the software's library or reference peptides. It is not a physical time and cannot be converted to seconds. |
| `unit` | `unknown` | The evidence does not establish it. |

## `confidence_alpha`

- Keys mean the identification; `quantification_q_value` is the q-value of the quantified signal, such as Sage's MS1 peak
- `q_value` in `layers` is per run, in `var` across the whole experiment
- Left out: scores, vendor summaries, and protein-level confidence of vendors other than DIA-NN, Spectronaut and MaxQuant

<!-- generated by scripts/coverage_tables.py: confidence_alpha -->

### Vocabulary

| Qualifier | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `pep` | Posterior error probability: the probability that this single identification is wrong; lower is better. |
| `kind` | `q_value` | The smallest false discovery rate at which this identification, or quantified signal, is accepted; lower is better. In layers per run; in var across the whole experiment. |
| `kind` | `library_q_value` | The q-value of the identification's spectral-library entry, built across all runs; lower is better. |
| `stage` | `identification` | Whether the level's entity is correctly identified. |
| `stage` | `quantification` | Whether the signal quantified for it, such as its MS1 peak, belongs to it. |

### Keys

| Key | Kind | Stage | PSI-MS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q_value` | `q_value` | `identification` |  |
| `pep` | `pep` | `identification` |  |
| `library_q_value` | `library_q_value` | `identification` |  |
| `quantification_q_value` | `q_value` | `quantification` |  |

## `fasta_peptides_alpha`

- Fields apb-fasta writes into the `fasta_validation` varm table that a consumer reads; a result answers them once `apb-fasta verify-peptides` has run
- Naming the set on a result apb-fasta has not verified raises when the catalog opens, saying what to run; `DataCatalog.answering_sets(result)` lists the sets that open

<!-- generated by scripts/coverage_tables.py: fasta_peptides_alpha -->

### Vocabulary

| Qualifier | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `peptide_in_fasta` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: The stripped sequence occurs in at least one FASTA protein. |
| `kind` | `fasta_matching_protein_count` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: Distinct FASTA proteins containing the sequence. |
| `kind` | `fasta_matching_protein_ids` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: The ';'-joined FASTA ids of the matching proteins. |
| `kind` | `fasta_matching_organisms` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: Sorted, ';'-joined organism mnemonics of the matching proteins, e.g. HUMAN;YEAST. |
| `kind` | `fasta_matches_contaminant` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: A matching FASTA protein is a contaminant. |
| `kind` | `reported_member_organisms` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: Sorted, ';'-joined organism mnemonics of the reported members found; null when the level reports no protein group. |
| `kind` | `reported_members_contaminant` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: A reported member found in the FASTA is a contaminant; null when the level reports no protein group. |
| `kind` | `reported_leading_id` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: FASTA id of the leading protein, the first member of protein_assignment. |
| `kind` | `reported_leading_accession` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's accession. |
| `kind` | `reported_leading_description` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's header text after the id. |
| `kind` | `reported_leading_gene_name` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's gene name. |
| `kind` | `reported_leading_protein_length` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's sequence length. |
| `kind` | `reported_leading_tryptic_peptides` | apb-fasta's peptide verification: The leading protein's tryptic peptides of 7 to 29 residues, cleaved after K or R unless P follows. |
